text:
Isha Mehta: FYI from afternoon sync  need to finalize R3 slice. Customers want clear win: batching, caching hints, quant guidance, and eval-based alerts. We must minimize runtime risk.
Noah Green: Agreed. My proposal: prioritize features by deploy risk and customer value. Batching = highest value but highest risk; caching hints & quant = low risk advisories; eval-alerts = middle (read-only first).
Ava Patel: For batching, we should limit to two safe modes: 'latency-safe' (small max batch, strict p99 cap) and 'throughput' (larger batches, higher util). Each mode must have instant rollback via feature flag.
Rahul Singh: Telemetry requirements: for each suggestion/applied rule emit event tags: opt.r3.suggestion, opt.r3.applied, opt.r3.alert. Include rule_id, route, before_tokens, after_tokens_est, latency_p95_before.
Isha Mehta: Acceptance criteria idea: - Pilot with 3 customers, - Console shows per-route token savings + latency deltas, - p99 regression <= 10% for customers who enable batching, - advisory recs include templated rationale + audit row, - eval-alert false positive rate <8% in pilot.
Noah Green: Add gating: per-customer toggle, X% canary rollout, and an SLO rollback rule if p99 increases by >10% for 5m window.
Ava Patel: Implementation note: avoid per-request quant switching. Serve quant recs as a report/API only. If customers want auto-switch later, that's separate project.
Rahul Singh: For auditability, we can store recommendation meta in the events table and provide CSV export. That should satisfy FinReg customers for pilot.
Isha Mehta: Owners: runtime = Ava, telemetry = Rahul, Console = Noah. I'll coordinate pilots and documentation.
Noah Green: Timeline (4 weeks): W1: rule schema + DSL draft, W2: runtime prototype (heuristics) + perf baseline, W3: telemetry hook + Console stub, W4: pilot rollouts and metrics review.
Ava Patel: Blocker: kernel-level batching optimization might be blocked by eng-runtime capacity. If so, we'll ship user-space scheduler hooking into existing runtime and mark optimizations for follow-up.
Rahul Singh: Ops ask: prep alert runbook and clear escalation path. Also capture contact for pilot customers to report perceived regressions.
Isha Mehta: Quick decision required: do we hard-enable batching for pilot customers or keep it opt-in? My preference: opt-in with recommended default for certain routes.
Noah Green: Vote: opt-in with recommended default. Gives safety and adoption nudge.
Ava Patel: Will prototype two heuristics: sticky-prefix and opportunistic micro-batching. Delivery by end of W2 with perf numbers.
Rahul Singh: I'll add telemetry events to backlog and create the sample dashboard tiles for Console: token-savings, p50/p95/p99 latency, alerts-fired.
tooling-bot: Poll created "R3 rollout stance" options: [opt-in-recommended, hard-enable, read-only-advisory] Vote at https://redwood.internal/poll/10234
Noah Green: +1 opt-in-recommended
Isha Mehta: Final call: R3 MVP = batching heuristics (opt-in w/ recommended default), cache/quant as advisory outputs with templated rationale + audit rows, eval-triggered alerts read-only in Console. Owners and timeline as above.
Ava Patel: :thumbsup:
Rahul Singh: :white_check_mark:
Noah Green: :rocket:
